source.description:
GOAL: Make xtrm-tools CI/CD contract-dependent on specialists before considering a monorepo. xtrm-tools owns the Category B filesystem payload users receive through xt install/update, so it must prove that payload matches the expected specialists package/source and works on a fresh machine.

WHY: Fresh-machine failures showed xtrm-tools was the distribution choke point: using-specialists-v3 existed in specialists but was not vendored here; update-specialists source changed in specialists but mirror/registry required a separate xtrm-tools commit; npm latest lag means users do not receive pushed source fixes until xtrm-tools is released.

SUCCESS: xtrm-tools CI fails on stale vendored specialists skills, stale .xtrm/registry.json, missing required default skills, invalid package payload, or fresh-machine xt doctor/update failures. Release pipeline records which specialists package/SHA generated the payload.

SCOPE: xtrm-tools vendor script, registry generation, pack payload validation, fresh-machine smoke with packed xtrm-tools + specialists, release gate/version pin. Specialists owns its package payload/runtime contract in unitAI-ye5s9.

NON_GOAL: Do not move to monorepo yet. This epic adds split-repo contract hardening first.
source.title: Epic: harden xtrm-tools ↔ specialists release contract

source.description:
## What implementation this covers

Covers implementation issue xtrm-9xg2.2 (CI + pack guards for flat active layout).

## Layer classification

Boundary layer. This work validates filesystem/package/CI contracts at repo → packed artifact seam and at source-tree scan boundary.

## Strategy chosen

Contract tests and smoke checks, live-first within local CI:
- inspect real `npm pack` file list
- run real source scan script against tracked files
- assert approved ignore/transient paths are only exceptions

## Test file structure

Prefer one focused test surface plus one CI invocation:
- script-level test under existing CLI/workflow test area if helper is scripted
- workflow smoke step in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`
- fixtures for allowlisted historical/transient paths if needed

## What to assert

- Packed tarball does not contain `.xtrm/skills/active/**`.
- Guard fails on synthetic `active/claude` / `active/pi` references outside allowlist.
- Guard passes for explicitly declared transient/historical paths only.
- Guard output mentions canonical `.xtrm/skills/active` / `.xtrm/hooks/` contract.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Boundary contract checks cover real pack output, not mocked file lists.
- [ ] Source-scan regression case proves stale runtime-tier paths fail CI.
- [ ] Allowlist behavior is asserted with concrete fixtures/examples.
- [ ] Test docs/name reference xtrm-9xg2.2 and updated canonical layout.

Shell layer. This work validates user-facing command output and end-to-end runtime wiring across init/doctor/update surfaces.

CLI integration tests and smoke tests:
- invoke real command constructors or CLI wrappers
- assert runtime-view output/messages use flat active path only
- verify failure text treats per-runtime tiers as legacy/invalid

Extend existing shell-facing suites:
- `cli/test/doctor.test.ts`
- `cli/src/tests/update.test.ts`
- `cli/test/skills-runtime-sync.test.ts`
- add/adjust init or clean command assertions where message drift exists

## What to assert

- `xt doctor` JSON/text reports flat active view readiness only.
- `xt update` smoke output and JSON continue working with canonical flat path wiring.
- init/clean/user-facing strings no longer print `active/{claude,pi}`.
- Legacy per-runtime directory scenarios are handled as invalid drift, not expected layout.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Shell/integration coverage exercises doctor + update flat-layout behavior.
- [ ] Regression assertions catch stale `active/claude` / `active/pi` wording in command output.
- [ ] Tests reference xtrm-9xg2.1 and xtrm-9xg2.3.
